interpretation.title: CRM Cloud Migration Plan
interpretation.audience: Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and senior leadership
interpretation.objective: Outline a detailed, low‑budget migration strategy to move the existing CRM to the cloud within 6 weeks while ensuring zero downtime
missing_info: Current on‑premises CRM platform and version
Total budget amount allocated for the migration
Target cloud provider or preferred cloud environment
Compliance or security requirements (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA)
Key integration points with other systems
Available internal resources and skill sets
conflicts: Tight budget vs. aggressive 6‑week timeline with zero‑downtime requirement
assumptions: Number of users to be confirmed by requester; plan will use a scalable licensing model
Current CRM is a common enterprise solution (e.g., Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, or a custom app) and will be treated generically
Budget is limited; plan emphasizes cost‑effective, open‑source tools and existing staff effort
Target cloud provider not yet chosen; plan remains provider‑agnostic with options for major IaaS providers
Compliance requirements are standard industry regulations; plan includes generic security controls
Integrations are limited to typical systems (email, ERP, analytics) and will be addressed via API gateways
Internal team includes at least one cloud‑savvy engineer and a project manager; additional resources will be sourced as needed

plan.description: Provide a concise overview of the migration goal, constraints, and key success criteria.
plan.instructions: Summarize the objective (move CRM to cloud in 6 weeks with zero downtime), tight‑budget constraint, major assumptions, and the high‑level approach.

plan.description: Define what is in scope and out of scope for the migration.
plan.instructions: List in‑scope items (CRM data, user access, integrations, security controls) and out‑of‑scope items (non‑CRM systems, long‑term optimization). Reference the key facts and assumptions.

plan.description: Describe the migration methodology and zero‑downtime technique.
plan.instructions: Detail a phased lift‑and‑shift with data replication, DNS failover, and cut‑over rehearsal. Include steps: discovery, environment set‑up, pilot, full sync, cut‑over, validation. Emphasize use of existing staff and open‑source tools.

plan.description: Show the 6‑week schedule with major milestones and deliverables.
plan.instructions: Create a week‑by‑week Gantt‑style table (Week 1‑6) listing tasks, owners, and estimated effort. Label the dates as estimates.

plan.description: Outline required resources, roles, and a rough cost estimate.
plan.instructions: Provide a table with personnel (PM, cloud engineer, DBA, tester), cloud services (compute, storage, networking), and licensing costs. Mark all figures as estimates and note the tight‑budget focus.

plan.description: Identify major risks, their impact, likelihood, and mitigation actions.
plan.instructions: Create a risk matrix table covering the budget‑timeline conflict, data sync issues, compliance gaps, and resource constraints. Include mitigation strategies.

plan.description: Capture all assumptions, open questions, and any unresolved conflicts.
plan.instructions: List each assumption from the analysis, the missing information items, and propose a trade‑off approach for the budget vs. timeline conflict (e.g., phased rollout or additional temporary staffing).
